items.evidence: play --ticks 1 (both on <runs>/night-engine-3 and on .../work as the README writes it) printed screen title and one JSON object with all 23 keys the brief names (tick, screen, menu_index, volume, difficulty, texts, cursor, piece, stock, grid, slot, slots, clock, speed, coins, served, lost, queue, customers, arrivals, replaying, replay_ready, ledger).
--frame f.png --size 800x480 after runs on title, settings, ledger, layout, night, paused, summary: each a valid PNG, header says 800 x 480; README's own frame command also wrote frame.png.
Fresh run: texts [Night Market, Layout, Ledger, Settings, Quit], menu_index 0; up at 0 stays 0, downs go 1,2,3 and stay 3 (also with down on consecutive ticks).

Settings: Volume: 5 at first, rights to 10 and stays 10, lefts to 0 and stays 0; difficulty Normal -> right Hard, stays Hard, left Normal, Easy, stays Easy; texts 'Volume: N', 'Difficulty: Normal'; escape -> screen title.
Run with --settings k1 set volume 4, difficulty hard; second run on k1 starts volume 4, hard; a fresh folder starts 5, normal.
0:enter on fresh place: screen layout, cursor (0,0), piece stove, slot 1, stock 3/4/2, grid [], texts Layout, Piece: Stove, Slot: 1, Stove: 3, Table: 4, Lamp: 2, plus Enter/Escape lines.

With 'none' between words the cursor moves one cell each way (up raises y) and stops at x 0/7, y 0/4, menu_index unchanged, screen stays layout. But 0:enter,2:right,3:right,4:right leaves cursor at (1,0), not (3,0): the same word given again without a different word between counts once (README admits it), against the brief's 'each acts once ... even when the same word was given at the tick before'.

With none between: next_piece table, lamp, stove; prev_piece lamp, table, stove; Piece: text follows. But 2:next_piece,12:next_piece (ten ticks apart, no other word between) gives table, not lamp; 2:next_piece,4:next_piece,6:next_piece stays table. Repeated words are swallowed, so the cycle does not happen with a plain script.
Stoves placed at (0,0),(1,0),(2,0) stock 3->0; 4th stove at (3,0) changes nothing; table on occupied (2,0) changes nothing; 4 tables placed, 5th at (0,4) nothing; 2 lamps placed, 3rd nothing.
place stove at (0,0) Stove: 2; erase on empty (1,0) nothing; erase at (0,0) -> grid [], stock stove 3, text 'Stove: 3'.
Built stove(0,0), table(1,0), cursor (1,1), escape -> title, enter -> layout with same grid, cursor (0,0); later run on same --settings: layout shows same grid, stock 2/3/2.

With none between: next_slot 1->2->3->1, save_slot copies grid and leaves it, load_slot on empty slot 2 nothing, load_slot slot 1 restores grid and stock (table 3->4). But 2:next_slot,3:next_slot gives slot 2, not 3: the repeated word counts once, so the cycle fails with a plain script.
Later run on the same folder showed the same three slots; next_slot then load_slot gave slot 2's grid stove(0,0), table(1,0), stock table 3.

Only a stove: enter -> layout, texts gain 'Needs a stove and a table', gone after next word; with stove+table: screen night, clock 0, speed slow, coins/served/lost 0, grid unchanged, '18:00', 'Speed: Slow'.

Night started at tick 9: slow clock 0 at 32, 1 at 33, 2 at 57; fast from tick 10: clock 1 at tick 16, 2 at 22; stop: clock 0 at tick 399, screen night; slow 12 ticks then fast: clock 1 at tick 24 (progress kept). Texts 18:01 etc., 'Speed: Fast' follow.
Seed 1 [5,12,18,23,33,...,356], seed 2 [5,9,13,...,356], seed 1 again identical, seed 7 different ending 359; gaps 4 to 10, all under 360; seed 2 list same at clock 0 and at clock 248.

My own simulator of the brief compared per minute (coins, served, lost, queue, every customer's id/state/x/y/wait) with the game over 360 minutes for 4 layouts and difficulties: 0 mismatches. Single-table run: 4th waiting customer turned away, lost 1 at minute 34, queued x/y null.
stove(1,0)+table(0,0): customer 1 cooking at minute 5, eating at 25; stove(3,0)+table(0,0): cooking till 34, eating at 35.
Adjacent case: paid at minute 35 (10 after eating at 25), coins 8, served 1, table taken by next; with a lamp at (0,1) beside the table coins 12; not adjacent: pays 8 at 45.

Hard, stove(3,0) table(0,0): at minute 35 customer 1 gone, lost 1->2, coins 0, and customer 2 already seated and cooking at (0,0) that minute (table and stove freed at once). Easy/normal/hard full nights match my simulator at patience 60/40/30.
Normal adjacent: minute 35 customer 1 pays and customer 2 (front of queue) is cooking at (0,0) the same minute; per-minute comparison with my simulator found 0 mismatches.
At clock 360 screen summary, texts Night over, Coins: 176, Served: 17, Lost: 27, Enter: title matching state and my simulator (which gives nothing for those still in the stall); enter -> title.
Same layout, seed 11, normal: slow, fast, and a run mixing fast/stop/slow/fast/stop/fast/slow/fast all ended 64 coins, 6 served, 39 lost.

Escape at clock 4: screen paused, texts Paused, Resume, Title; clock stays 4 for 200 ticks; Enter on Resume and later Escape both resume from the same clock; Title (down, enter) -> title, ledger unchanged and replay still the earlier night (replay gave 140/14/29).
Fresh ledger screen: 'No nights yet'. After night: ledger [{176,17,27,normal}], Ledger screen 'Coins 176, served 17, lost 27, Normal'; a later run on the same folder shows it too.
Four nights (176, 136, 160, 140): ledger then [140,160,136], the first gone, newest first; a night given up from the pause and two replays added nothing.
After the night title texts [Night Market, Layout, Replay, Ledger, Settings, Quit], replay_ready true; same in a later run on the same folder.

Night seed 3 normal (176/17/27); then with seed 9, difficulty hard and a changed grid, Replay: screen night, replaying true, texts start 'Replay', arrivals = seed 3 list, grid = night's grid; at 360 'Replay over', Coins 176, Served 17, Lost 27; ledger and replay unchanged afterwards.
Before that replay the grid was changed (erase), a slot saved and loaded, difficulty set to hard; replay still played the kept grid and gave the same 176/17/27; again from a later run with seed 4.
Two runs seed 6, same script, each from its own copy of the same kept folder: outputs byte-identical; seed 12 gives a different arrivals list.

Layout frame: 8x5 grid, stoves red with orange core, tables brown, lamps dark with yellow core at the cells the state lists, cursor outlined at (4,2) as state says, panel shows Piece: Lamp, Slot: 2, stock 0/0/0.

Night frames: grid and pieces, two purple queued squares at left, green eating at (0,0), tan cooking at tables, cyan seated at (7,4) (other frame), matching state; panel Coins 40, Served 4, Lost 0, 19:13, Speed: Fast.
Title, settings, ledger, paused, summary frames show their texts; the chosen entry has a bright blue focus ring (Ledger on title, Difficulty in settings, Title in paused).

README has how to play, keeping (the --settings folder: settings.json with grid, slots, ledger, last night), and play/frame commands that I ran as written: they printed the summary JSON and wrote an 800x480 frame.png.

defects: Any input word given again without a different word in between is ignored (cursor words, next_piece, prev_piece, next_slot, place, erase, save/load, speed words), even many ticks apart; the brief requires each to act. The README admits this.
On the title and paused frames the first entry is always drawn filled blue (primary style) while the focus is shown only by a ring, so two entries look highlighted when the focus is not on the first.
menu_index is null on layout and night screens (the brief does not say what it should be there).
Cooking customers (tan on a brown table) are hard to tell from an empty table in the night frame.
